sanskrit_verse:
स्वभावोक्तं वचस् तेषां ग्राह्यं यद् दोषवर्जितम् ।
उक्ते तु साक्षिणो राज्ञा न पृष्टव्याः पुनः पुनः ॥
transliteration: svabhāvoktaṃ vacas teṣāṃ grāhyaṃ yad doṣavarjitam | ukte tu sākṣiṇo rājñā na pṛṣṭavyāḥ punaḥ punaḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: That speech which is in accordance with one's inherent nature and free from defect shall be accepted; once witnesses have spoken before the King, they must not be questioned repeatedly.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in the King as the witness-integrator of truthful testimony.
Causation aligns with svabhāva (inherent nature) rather than external compulsion.
Capacity-based responsibility requires that witnesses speak only what is uncontrived and faultless.
Restoration logic prevents re-traumatization through repetitive inquiry.
Consciousness alignment occurs when testimony flows naturally without coercion.
executable_legal_axioms: IF a witness delivers testimony aligned with their svabhāva AND the statement contains no internal contradiction OR defect, THEN accept the testimony as valid.
ONCE a witness has been heard by the King, DO NOT permit repeated questioning under any circumstance.
IF a witness shows signs of distress or inconsistency due to repetition, INITIATE restorative protocol for integrity reintegration.
ENSURE all judicial inquiries respect the svabhāva of the speaker to maintain pramāṇa purity.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that testimonial authenticity lies in spontaneous, defect-free utterance rooted in one’s svabhāva. Repeated interrogation undermines both truth-reception and consciousness stability. The court must recognize natural testimony as superior evidence and enforce cessation of redundant witness recall.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa functions through direct perception and non-defective cognition. When a witness speaks from svabhāva, the causal chain remains untainted. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures sequential manifestation of dharma where truth emerges unforced. Responsibility is proportional to capacity—those who speak truly need not be subjected to coercive repetition. This aligns with non-punitive reality because justice arises through alignment, not imposition.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Implement svabhāva-validation protocols wherein testimony is assessed for coherence and spontaneity prior to acceptance.
Enforce cessation-of-repetition orders post-initial testimony to preserve mental clarity and prevent trauma recurrence.
Deploy consciousness-monitoring tools during hearings to detect stress-induced deviations from svabhāva flow.
Initiate completion rituals after testimony to restore energetic neutrality and dissolve residual tension.
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: testimony born of svabhāva, untouched by flaw, is the highest pramāṇa. Repetition is rejected to uphold consciousness integrity. Thus dharma is restored, reality affirmed as non-punitive, and consciousness declared the supreme adjudicator.
